confirmed.title: Manager PINs can be guessed without limit: no throttle, lockout, audit or alert on wrong PINs, and every void, cancel, refund and comp now rests on that PIN
confirmed.repro: As cashier1 (OTP session), ring an order with 2 lines. Send POST /pos/orders/:id/void {orderItemId:<line 2>, reason:'x', managerOverridePin:'<guess>'} 200 times (20 in parallel per batch) with PINs 200000..200199. Then send the real FOH manager PIN.
confirmed.expected: Wrong manager PINs are rate-limited per cashier/device (lockout after a few failures, like the login limiter), each failure is audited, and repeated failures raise an exception flag for the owner. The CLAUDE.md §17.4 separation of duties ('a cashier or server can never void alone') depends on the PIN staying secret.
confirmed.actual: All 200 guesses return 403 INVALID_MANAGER_PIN, at about 5 guesses per second (38.8 s for 200), with 0 exception flags and 0 audit rows. The real PIN is accepted immediately afterwards (200). PINs may be 4 digits (PIN_FORMAT 4–8), and a guess matches ANY manager of the company, including the CEO's PIN. At this rate a 4-digit PIN falls in well under an hour of background requests from a cashier token. The same unthrottled check sits behind the discount override, cash pay-outs, comps, refunds and order cancel.
confirmed.evidence: backend/.sim/foh-r2/13-pin.ts output: pin.burst {attempts:200, ms:38822, perSecond:5, codes:{INVALID_MANAGER_PIN:200}}; pin.trail {exceptions:0, audits:[]}; pin.correctAfterBurst 200. Also 12-more.ts: 15 sequential wrong PINs, then the correct PIN is accepted.
confirmed.suspectedCause: backend/src/modules/auth/managerPin.ts:56-76 (verifyManagerPin loops bcrypt.compare over every manager of the company with no attempt counter); callers requireManagerApproval (backend/src/modules/pos/service.ts:1436-1453), ensureCapOrManagerOverride (:1388) and the discount gate (:202) never record failures.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Count failed manager-PIN attempts per actor (and per order) in the redisFast-backed limiter used for login (e.g. 5 per 15 min), then return 429 MANAGER_PIN_LOCKED. Audit 'manager_pin.failed' with the actor and order, flag an exception for the company after N failures, and consider requiring 6+ digit manager PINs.

verdict.reason:
The finding is real, and it is not one of the intended changes. §17.4 says a wrong PIN gets a 403 INVALID_MANAGER_PIN. It does not say guesses are unlimited, and the isWeakPin comment in managerPin.ts says weak-PIN rejection is "Not a substitute for lockout". The code has a single verifier, verifyManagerPin (backend/src/modules/auth/managerPin.ts:56-76). It loads every active approver in the company and runs bcrypt.compare against each one. There is no attempt counter, no Redis call, no audit and no flag. None of its callers record failures either:
- requireManagerApproval (pos/service.ts:1436-1453), used by line void and /orders/:id/cancel
- ensureCapOrManagerOverride (:1388-1427), used by refund, comp and void caps
- the discount and price-override gates (:202, :225)
- staff meal (:1964)
- till pay-out (:2981)
- trustops petty cash (trustops/routes.ts:342)

Other secrets in the same codebase are throttled. The HR kiosk PIN locks after 5 tries in 15 minutes (hr/kioskPin.ts:20). The self-service PIN change is limited to 5 and 6 attempts, and its comment says that is exactly to stop "grinding the 10^4 PIN space" (auth/routes.ts:94-99). The manager-override PIN is the most powerful of these and has no limit at all.

The only brake is the global @fastify/rate-limit: 200 per minute (index.ts:260). It runs at onRequest, before requireAuth sets req.staffUser, so it is keyed on the client IP, not the user as the code comment claims. Changing IP gives a fresh bucket.

One correction to the original evidence: the sim's "5 guesses/s" was measured on loopback, which isInternalRequest exempts from the limiter. In production the ceiling is about 200 guesses per minute per public IP. That does not change the conclusion. About 9.8k non-weak 4-digit PINs at 200 per minute takes about 49 minutes worst case for one manager. Any approver's PIN matches, so with k approvers the expected time is roughly 49/(k+1) minutes, and less again with a second IP. 6-digit PINs (about 83 hours per IP) are allowed but not required.

I am keeping severity at high. The attacker must be an authenticated insider (cashier or server), but that is exactly the actor §17.4 exists to stop. The payoff is unattributed voids, cancels, refunds, comps, pay-outs and over-cap discounts, all recorded against a manager, including the CEO's PIN, which unlocks discounts above the manager cap. There is zero audit or alert trail of the guessing.
verdict.evidence:
I reproduced it with a vitest file kept at /home/user/servd/backend/.sim/foh-r2/verify/zzverify_foh_0.test.ts. To run it, I copied it to tests/ and deleted the copy afterwards. It ran against my own database, servd_test_rv_foh_0, created and later dropped. For Redis I used 6424/26, because 6379 only has 16 databases. Setup: two companies; company A has foh_management (PIN 5821), admin/CEO (PIN 6047) and a cashier; company B has its own manager.

Results:
1. Line void: 100 wrong 6-digit PINs (in parallel batches of 20) plus 5 wrong 4-digit PINs. Output: [rv.void.burst] {"attempts":105,"codes":{"INVALID_MANAGER_PIN":105},"auditsDuring":[],"flagsDuring":0}. The real PIN was then accepted: [rv.void.correctAfterBurst] 200 voided.
2. POST /orders/:id/cancel: 30 wrong PINs, then the CEO's PIN. Output: [rv.cancel.burst] {"codes":{"INVALID_MANAGER_PIN":30},"auditsDuring":0,"flagsDuring":0}; [rv.cancel.ceoPin] 200; audit order.cancel approverId equals the CEO. So a guess matches any approver of the company.
3. Company B's manager PIN at company A gives INVALID_MANAGER_PIN. Company separation holds; this is not part of the finding.
4. Global limiter with the production config: one public X-Forwarded-For IP gave {"INVALID_MANAGER_PIN":180,"RL_429":30}. The same cashier token from a second IP was not throttled (answered INVALID_MANAGER_PIN), which confirms the limiter is keyed per IP at onRequest (index.ts:256-270, plugin defaultHook 'onRequest'; requireAuth sets staffUser in preHandler, middleware.ts:128/157).
5. Redis db 26 held no keys after the run: the manager-PIN path never touches a limiter.

Code: managerPin.ts:56-76 has no counter; pos/service.ts:1419-1420, 1448-1450, 1964-1965 and 2981-2982 throw INVALID_MANAGER_PIN with no audit or flag. Compare hr/kioskPin.ts:20,46-53 (KIOSK_PIN_LIMIT 5/15min with recordFailure) and auth/routes.ts:94-99 (PIN_CHANGE limits, "stops a borrowed session grinding the 10^4 PIN space").

**Cause:** `revalueForBillVariance` (`backend/src/modules/accounting/supplierPosting.ts`, around lines 111-115) computes `share = min(onHand, billedQty)/billedQty` from the item's whole on-hand stock. It never looks at the PO line's `quantityReceived`. `billVarianceLines` takes the variance over the full billed quantity.

**Wrong result on billing:** Any billed quantity that has not arrived yet is treated as already used. The header comment assumes billed = received, and this case breaks it.

**Wrong result on void:** `postSupplierBillVoid` re-derives the share from stock on hand at void time. It does not reverse what the bill actually absorbed. After a later receipt, share goes from 0.8 to 1, so the void takes out more than was put in. It then books the excess to 5060 as "used since billed", although nothing was used.

- Roles were normal: buyer raised and submitted the PO, a manager who is not the raiser received it, and a manager billed and voided.
- The PO was approved and sent.
- Nothing in `createBill` or the route blocks billing more than was received. `matchBill` only reports it as a mismatch ("Billed 60, received 40").

confirmed.suspectedCause: backend/src/modules/crosschecks/routes.ts:182-184: prisma.recipe.findFirst({ where: { id: body.recipeId, kind: 'component' } }) has no company scope, and recipeId is written unchecked at :188.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds up, and it is not one of the intended behaviour changes. POST /crosschecks/prep-batches checks that each input stock item belongs to the active company, but it never checks recipeId. Line 183 in backend/src/modules/crosschecks/routes.ts runs `prisma.recipe.findFirst({ where: { id: body.recipeId, kind: 'component' } })` with no company filter. Line 188 then writes `recipeId: body.recipeId ?? null` unchecked, and any id is accepted, including one that doesn't exist. Recipe has no tenantId column, and the route never calls the existing company resolver `subRecipeIdsForCompany(tenantId)` from par-sheet/routes.ts. That breaks the CLAUDE.md rule "never trust an id from the client … cross-company attach on create → 422". The setup is not at fault: cookB is a plain `kitchen` user in company B, the route allows ALL_STAFF, and /crosschecks has no module gate.

I lowered severity from medium to low:
(a) Nothing leaks into company A. A's par sheet keeps 0 batches for its sub-recipe, because batchesForDay filters batches by which company owns the input items. A's GET /prep-batches does not list B's batch, and the yield exception is stamped with B.
(b) The stock damage stays inside company B. The skipped draw of B's flour is never taken later either, because B's plates never use A's sub-recipe. B's stock stays overstated until the next physical count, which then records it as shrinkage.
(c) A B cook can get the same "batch that draws no stock" with B's own sub-recipe ids. Inputs are never matched against the recipe's ingredients, so citing a B component with unrelated ingredients has the same effect. Crossing companies only adds a cross-company reference in the data.
(d) A's sub-recipe ids are not listed to B users. Exploiting this needs a leaked id, or a shared-staff login that belongs to both companies.

It is still a real company-separation defect under the standing rule. The fix: resolve recipeId through `subRecipeIdsForCompany(tenantId)` and return 422 otherwise, and ideally also check the inputs against the recipe.
verdict.evidence:
I reproduced it with a temporary vitest file, /home/user/servd/backend/.sim/boh-r2/verify/zzverify_boh_3.test.ts, using config vitest.boh3.config.ts in the same folder. It ran against its own database, servd_test_rv_boh_3, created for the run and dropped afterwards. Nothing was placed in tests/ and no tracked file was changed. The Redis db 29 setting failed with "DB index is out of range", but this route does not use Redis.

Setup: two companies. Company A has the 'Flipd smash sauce' sub-recipe, used by a Flipd plate; subRecipeIdsForCompany(A) contains it and subRecipeIdsForCompany(B) does not. Company B has Atta at 70 kg and its own 'Viva dough' sub-recipe used by its Naan plate. The caller is a company B user with role 'kitchen'.

Results:
- Batch citing A's sub-recipe: 201, the stored recipeId is A's sub-recipe, the batch is stamped with company B, and flour stays 70 -> 70 (nothing drawn).
- Same batch with no recipe: 201, flour 70 -> 68.
- Batch citing B's own sub-recipe: 201, flour 68 -> 68. Skipping the draw here is by design.
- Batch citing a random, non-existent UUID: 201, the bogus id is stored, flour 68 -> 66.
- Company A's par sheet: A's sub-recipe shows 0 batches.
- Company B's par sheet: B's own sub-recipe shows 1 batch.
- Company A's GET /crosschecks/prep-batches does not include B's batch.

Code: backend/src/modules/crosschecks/routes.ts lines 182-184 (the lookup has no company filter) and line 188 (recipeId stored unchecked); the scoped helper is subRecipeIdsForCompany in backend/src/modules/par-sheet/routes.ts:39.
